episode_title: How to launch a multi-line consortium that brokers want to use, with Tom Squires and Dan Prince

real_qa.q: How does the Augentic multi-line consortium model allow brokers to access Aegis London capacity without changing their workflow?
real_qa.r: Day one, the broker collects Aegis terms through face-to-face negotiation or email as they normally would. They forward those terms and submission to Augentic by email. The system ingests and structures the data in the background, housing the rules of the digital consortium, and quickly responds to the broker saying they can boost Aegis's line with extra capacity. The broker then has a choice of how much consortium line to take, and can email back to firm order the policy through their placing platform of choice—no change to current workflow, just an efficient method of gathering extra capacity.
real_qa.requete: Augentic multi-line consortium Aegis broker workflow

real_qa.q: Why do facilities historically fail when markets harden and what is the cycle that keeps repeating?
real_qa.r: In a soft market, people look to keep their top line growing, but if you grow into a soft market, it is extremely difficult to maintain bottom line performance. People start losing money, the market contracts, and facilities are the first areas to lose out and shrink. Underwriters want to bring control back, and ultimately the expense ratio bites, claims come in, and people historically say enough is enough and focus back on open market underwriting.
real_qa.requete: why facilities fail hard market cycle insurance

real_qa.q: What did the recent LMA report reveal about the difference between lead and follow syndicate roles in the Lloyd's market?
real_qa.r: The LMA report defined the differences between lead and follow, showing you cannot categorize it simply as leader or follower. The report highlighted the evolution of true leaders and the emergence of portfolio solutions leaders who carry a panel of portfolio underwriters behind them. There was a massive mismatch where carriers see themselves as relevant but brokers perceive relevance differently—brokers value carriers who stand up and wow their clients in meetings, stick by them on large losses, and are truly there for them.
real_qa.requete: LMA report lead follow syndicate roles Lloyd's

real_qa.q: Why is Aegis London uniquely suited as a partner for Augentic's multi-line consortium compared to other syndicates?
real_qa.r: Aegis London has a high level of trust across all lines of business, which is fundamental to the play. Aegis also doesn't traditionally max out their line size with reinsurance when the market cycle changes. The modest line size deployment of Aegis through the cycle lends itself to being beneficial for brokers to have a boost behind the Aegis line. It was the combination of factors—being a trusted underwriter across the full board, maintaining discipline through cycles, and planning strategy five years ahead—that made Aegis the perfect partner.
real_qa.requete: why Aegis London multi-line consortium Augentic partner

real_qa.q: What is the leaders fee model in the Augentic consortium and why should market leaders be compensated for their work?
real_qa.r: The model includes a small leaders fee, which has been debated for years. The cost of leadership is constantly rising due to increased costs for people, travel, finding loss adjusters, getting the right data for claims, risk prevention through strong risk engineering, and the technicality of underwriting in an ever more complex world. True leaders fulfill exceptional service in claims handling, client relationships, and risk management, and there is real value and compensation due for it.
real_qa.requete: leaders fee compensation Augentic consortium market leaders

real_qa.q: How important is claims service in broker and client decision-making when selecting syndicates?
real_qa.r: Claims service importance varies by client size. At the commodity end of the market, clients focus primarily on price. However, for large risk managed clients who have experienced the difference between good and bad claims service, they ask the right questions. Brokers are more forthright in positioning markets with exceptional claims handling experience. In RFPs for large clients, brokers really push claims service as a differentiator that will be discussed with their client.
real_qa.requete: claims service importance broker syndicate selection insurance
